types.explanation: System status, or system help reply (RFC 5321 §4.2.2).
Help message (information on how to use the receiver or the meaning of a particular non-standard command; useful only to the human user).
<domain> Service ready (connection greeting).
<domain> Service closing transmission channel.
Requested mail action okay, completed (success).
User not local; will forward to <forward-path> (contains machine-parseable forwarding address).
Cannot VRFY user, but will accept message and attempt delivery.
Start mail input; end with <CRLF>.<CRLF> (intermediate reply for DATA).
<domain> Service not available, closing transmission channel (may be reply to any command; includes shutdown reason).
Requested mail action not taken: mailbox unavailable (e.g., busy or temporarily blocked).
Requested action aborted: local error in processing.
Requested action not taken: insufficient system storage.
Server unable to accommodate parameters.
Syntax error, command unrecognized (includes command line too long).
Syntax error in parameters or arguments.
Command not implemented.
Bad sequence of commands.
Command parameter not implemented.
Requested action not taken: mailbox unavailable (e.g., not found, no access, or command rejected for policy reasons).
User not local; please try <forward-path> (contains machine-parseable forwarding address).
Requested mail action aborted: exceeded storage allocation.
Requested action not taken: mailbox name not allowed (e.g., mailbox syntax incorrect).
Transaction failed (or, in connection-opening response, 'No SMTP service here').
MAIL FROM/RCPT TO parameters not recognized or not implemented.
